title: Opatija with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Hotels, Rules
metaDescription: Opatija with a dog: two dog beaches on the Lungomare, hotel pet fees of €0–40 per night, best months, vet basics and EU pet entry rules.
content:
## Dog Beaches in Opatija: Where Dogs Can Swim

Opatija has one official dog beach (plaža za pse). It lies on the Lungomare promenade between Opatija and Ičići, near Punta Kolova. A fence and gate separate it from the promenade, and natural barriers separate it from neighbouring areas. It has a dog shower and hygiene facilities. The beach is small and pebbly, with a listed capacity of about 50 bathers. A free-standing hose provides fresh water for rinsing and refilling bowls.

The second option is a small pebble beach below Villa Frappart in Lovran. It lies just past the village of Ika on the Lungomare and is marked as pet-friendly. Both beaches are free, and neither has a lifeguard.

This is enough for a short stay but not for a beach-focused holiday. Neither beach has the sun loungers, cafés or sandy entries found elsewhere on the Adriatic. Bring a dog mat and your own shade, and carry water.

## Are Dogs Allowed on Other Beaches in Opatija?

No. Central beaches such as Slatina are concrete bathing platforms where dogs are not allowed. The same applies to most hotel and municipal beaches along the riviera. Some small rocky spots outside the main bathing areas are tolerated by locals. Check for signs, because a missing sign does not mean permission.

## Dogs in the Old Town, Parks and on the Lungomare

Opatija is a seaside resort of villas and parks, not a walled old town. Leashed dogs can walk all 12 km of the Lungomare, from Volosko past Opatija to Lovran. Park Angiolina and the streets around it are also fine on a lead. Many cafés on the promenade and in the centre will bring a water bowl.

The Lungomare is narrow in places, with stairs and sea-level sections. Summer afternoons bring crowds, so a short leash works better than a flexi-lead. The best time for a long walk is before 9:00 or after 18:00.

## Dogs in Restaurants and Cafés

Terraces are the standard. Most restaurants and cafés in Opatija, Volosko and Lovran accept a leashed dog outdoors, especially at quieter times. Indoor dining is at the owner's discretion, and many venues refuse it. Ask before sitting down. A dog under the table is rarely a problem on a terrace, but a busy lunchtime in August is a different matter.

## National Parks and Nature Parks Nearby

Opatija has no national park, but Učka Nature Park rises directly behind the town. Leashed dogs are generally welcome on its trails. The summit, Vojak, is at 1,401 m, and the views over Kvarner are the main reward. Choose cooler months for the climb, and carry water for the dog because springs are scarce. Croatia's national parks, such as Plitvice and Krka, are a day trip or more away and have strict dog rules. Check the individual park's rules before going.

## Ferries, Catamarans and Boats

Opatija has no car ferry. Island trips to Cres and Lošinj leave from Brestova, around 30 km south-west of Opatija, on the Brestova–Porozina car ferry. Dogs are normally allowed on car ferries, on deck or in the vehicle, depending on the operator. Catamarans and excursion boats set their own rules: small dogs are often accepted, while larger dogs may need a muzzle and a lead. Confirm with the operator when booking. Don't assume a dog is welcome on a boat tour.

## Accommodation Pet Fees in Opatija

Typical hotel pet fees run from €10 to €40 per pet per night. Bristol charges about €10 in designated rooms, Hotel Lungomare about €13.50, Amadria Park Agava and Astoria about €20, Hotel Admiral about €25 (maximum two dogs up to 25 kg), Bellevue and Imperial about €35, and Bevanda about €40. Some hotels list no pet fee at all, and some private apartments charge €5–15 per night or a flat fee per stay. Fees change by season, so check before booking. Many hotels limit dogs to certain rooms and don't allow them in restaurants, pools or beach areas.

An apartment with a terrace or garden is often easier for a dog than a hotel room. Ask about the size limit, extra cleaning fees and whether the dog may be left alone.

## Summer Heat and Best Months

July and August bring temperatures around 28–31°C, and pavements and concrete platforms get very hot. Dogs overheat quickly, and the Lungomare offers shade only in parts. The best months are April to June and September to October. The sea is warm enough for swimming from late May to October, and the crowds are smaller. Winter is mild and fine for walking, but the dog beach is unlikely to be used.

## Vet Basics in Opatija

Opatija and neighbouring Matulji and Lovran have small-animal vets. Rijeka, about 15 km away, has the larger clinics and the most reliable out-of-hours care. Save the address of an emergency vet before travelling. Bring your dog's vaccination records, any regular medication and a basic first-aid kit. Tick prevention is sensible in Učka and any wooded areas. Dogs must be leashed in public places, and owners must pick up waste.

## EU Pet Passport Rules for Driving into Croatia

Croatia is in the EU, so the standard EU rules apply:

- **Microchip:** ISO-compatible, implanted before the rabies vaccination.
- **Rabies vaccination:** given at least 21 days before travel and kept valid.
- **Documents:** an EU pet passport, or an animal health certificate for dogs from outside the EU.
- **Limit:** a maximum of five pets per traveller on non-commercial trips.
- **Dogs from outside the EU:** must enter through a designated travel point and may need checks on arrival.

A tapeworm treatment is required only for entry into Finland, Ireland, Malta and Northern Ireland, which matters when returning from Croatia. Check current rules for your own route and country, as requirements change.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Opatija?

Opatija is moderately to very dog-friendly. It is excellent for walking, with a 12 km flat promenade, forest trails and a fenced dog beach. It is weak for beach days: two small dog beaches cannot replace a full beach holiday. The popular idea that a dog can follow you to the main sea platforms is wrong, and it quickly leads to a fine or an argument. The solution is simple: use the Punta Kolova dog beach early in the day, keep afternoons for shade, and choose spring or autumn. Rating: 4 out of 5 for a walking holiday, 3 out of 5 for a beach holiday.

faq.question: Is there a dog beach in Opatija?
faq.answer: Yes. The official dog beach is on the Lungomare between Opatija and Ičići, near Punta Kolova. It is fenced, has a gate and a dog shower, and is free. A second small dog beach is below Villa Frappart in Lovran.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on Opatija's main beaches?
faq.answer: No. Central beaches such as Slatina are concrete bathing platforms that ban dogs. Use the designated dog beaches or look for signs saying dogs are allowed.

faq.question: How much do hotels in Opatija charge for a dog?
faq.answer: Most hotels charge about €10–40 per pet per night. Examples include about €10 at Bristol, €20 at Astoria and Amadria Park Agava, and €25 at Admiral. Some hotels and apartments charge nothing or a small flat fee.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Opatija with a dog?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October are best. Temperatures are comfortable and the sea is warm enough from late May. July and August reach 28–31°C, so walks must be early or late.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia by car?
faq.answer: A dog needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport or health certificate. The limit is five pets per traveller. Check the rules for your departure country and for the return journey.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in restaurants in Opatija?
faq.answer: Dogs are generally welcome on restaurant and café terraces if leashed. Indoor access is up to each venue, and many refuse it. Ask before sitting down.

quickAnswer: Opatija is dog-friendly. Dogs can swim at the fenced dog beach near Punta Kolova on the Lungomare and at a small beach in Lovran. Most town beaches ban dogs. Hotels charge about €10–40 per night, and many apartments charge less. Best months are April–June and September–October.
